summary.intent: Discuss Phase 65 ('SDK Write-Chain, Bin Re-link, and Invite Claim') to lock implementation decisions into 65-CONTEXT.md, then produce a full set of executable PLAN.md files via the GSD plan-phase workflow (research → plan → verify).
summary.outcome: All planning artifacts produced and committed: 65-CONTEXT.md, 65-DISCUSSION-LOG.md, 65-RESEARCH.md, 65-VALIDATION.md, 65-PATTERNS.md, and 65-01 through 65-07-PLAN.md (7 plans in 4 waves). Plan-checker returned 0 blockers; 2 warnings fixed inline. Requirements 4/4 and decisions 6/6 covered.

repo: Phase-62 codec (packages/core/src/node/seal.ts) already provides the full write-body surface — sealNode(node, readKey, writeKey), unsealNode(..., writeKey?), encodeWriteBody/decodeWriteBody, role 0x04. Phase 65 calls the codec; it does not rebuild primitives.

sealChildWriteKey/unsealChildWriteKey (role 0x04) are entirely absent — only the role 0x02 read variants (sealChildReadKey/unsealChildReadKey) exist. This is the dependency-zero blocker for the entire write plane (Plan 65-01).
claimInviteReadKey is already fully implemented (packages/sdk-core/src/share/grant.ts:184); Phase 65 invite-claim work is service wiring only, not a new primitive.
reWrapForRecipients has already been deleted from the sdk layer (Phase 63); the only remaining copy lives in apps/web and is a Phase 68 deletion target.
shared-write.ts is fully stubbed — every export throws 'not implemented — phase 65 (write-chain)' with ipnsPrivateKey: Uint8Array parameter already in the signature.
BinEntry.nodeRef?: Node exists (Phase 62) but originalFolderKeyEncrypted is already absent from the type; bin restore needs a new nodeReadKey: Uint8Array field captured at addToBin time.

The 'delete addShareKeys/reWrapForRecipients/encryptedChildKeys' ROADMAP line splits by layer across three phases: sdk-layer reWrapForRecipients gone (63), apps/api addShareKeys+encryptedChildKeys (66), apps/web reWrapForRecipients + client.ts addShareKeysFn type (68).
Write-revocation cascade direction is child-first/bottom-up: leaves get new k51 names first, then parents re-point upward to the share root.

Q3 authority model: when write-recipient C deletes/moves a node the owner independently sub-shared to D, C unlinks+bins with no cross-principal revoke attempt; D's grant is a documented residual exposure bounded by the owner's next online sync, re-derived from shares WHERE rootNodeId IN (destroyed subtree) — no new schema.

workflow: GSD planner reliably commits plans to a stray docs/plan-phase-N branch instead of the active feature branch; recovery is always a safe ff-merge onto feat/ followed by deleting the stray branch.
GSD commit helper false-negatives (returns commit_failed even when lint-staged completed cleanly and the commit landed); always verify with git log rather than retrying on the helper's result.
Plan-checker warnings that are one-line mechanical fixes (removing || true, adding RESOLVED markers) should be applied inline rather than spawning a full opus revision cycle.
A rejected or user-interrupted AskUserQuestion call followed by a re-invocation of the same command does NOT signal a preference for plain text; re-issue the structured question UI.
The Nyquist/VALIDATION.md scaffold must be committed explicitly after the researcher returns if a Validation Architecture section is present in RESEARCH.md — it is not auto-committed by any subagent.
PATTERNS.md is never auto-committed by the pattern-mapper subagent; the orchestrator must commit it explicitly before spawning the planner.

friction: AskUserQuestion was interrupted on the first discuss-phase invocation; on re-invocation the assistant incorrectly inferred the user preferred plain text and skipped structured questions, requiring user correction ('why are the questions being skipped?').
GSD commit helper false-negatived on every commit across the session (both discuss-phase and plan-phase) — required git log verification after each commit operation.
Planner created a stray docs/plan-phase-65 branch instead of committing directly to the feature branch, requiring a manual ff-merge recovery step.
The gsd_run JS syntax error (use of ?? and && operators) caused a parse failure in the coverage gate shell one-liner, requiring a second bash invocation to re-parse the result.
plan-phase workflow requires the orchestrator to explicitly commit both VALIDATION.md and PATTERNS.md — neither subagent does it automatically, and the gap is easy to miss.
